title: AlphaFold-Multimer-guided experiments corroborate six novel human protein interfaces
summary: Researchers developed a fragmentation strategy for AlphaFold-Multimer and applied it to 62 human protein interactions associated with neurological disorders. Eighteen predicted structures were judged correct or likely correct, and experiments corroborated six previously unreported interfaces: FBXO23–STX1B, STX1B–VAMP2, ESRRG–PSMC5, PEX3–PEX19, PEX3–PEX16 and SNRPB–GIGYF1.
organization: Institute of Molecular Biology Mainz, Hebrew University of Jerusalem and collaborators

evidence.tested: Eighteen predicted structures were judged correct or likely correct, and experiments corroborated six previously unreported interfaces: FBXO23–STX1B, STX1B–VAMP2, ESRRG–PSMC5, PEX3–PEX19, PEX3–PEX16 and SNRPB–GIGYF1.
evidence.unknown: The article reports 18 correct or likely correct models among 62 interactions and experimental support for six interfaces; these are not a comprehensive interactome map. AlphaFold-Multimer showed limited specificity and was sensitive to input-fragment length, as the source explicitly notes.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold-Multimer predicted domain–motif interface structures; researchers tested predictions and used the model-informed fragmentation strategy to prioritize interaction interfaces. Wet-lab assays corroborated six novel contacts, while the tool had limited specificity and performance declined with longer/full-length input sequences.
